anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685PW (U2) address strap is set with A0 (pin 1) tied to +3.3V while A1–A5 (pins 2,3,4,5,24) are tied to GND, and the sheet note explicitly reads 'I2C address: 0x41'. U2 SCL/SDA (pins 26/27) sit on I2C2_SCL_FCC/I2C2_SDA_FCC, the same bus as the INA219 (U1, note 'I2C address: 0x40').
anomalies.expected: The design specification's component table states the PWM/servo driver is 'NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40', i.e. all address pins strapped to GND (A0=0). The intended I2C address of the PCA9685 is 0x40, not 0x41.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40
FCC Peripherals sheet, U2 PCA9685PW, note 'I2C address: 0x41'; pin 1 A0 connected to +3.3V, pins 2-5 & 24 (A1-A5) to GND

anomalies.impact: The servo/PWM driver answers at 0x41 instead of the specified 0x40. Firmware written against the intended 0x40 address cannot enumerate or command the PCA9685, so the 16 PWM/servo outputs are never driven (loss of servo/control-surface actuation).

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the specified I2C address of the PCA9685 PWM driver: the schematic straps A0 high and annotates 0x41, whereas the specification defines the part at 0x40, which would leave the servo driver unaddressable by firmware expecting 0x40. All other power rails, MCU/sensor part identities, feedback divider (R5=6k8/R6=1k3 -> ~5 V), crystal/decoupling networks and FCC<->NAVC link (UART2/I2C/GPIO) trace consistently with the spec, including the documented barometer RESET/INT swap and the empty Sensors sheet.
